title: KHOU 11 Visits ELARA's Community Research
summary: A filmed interview at the Mamie George Community Center highlighted work with older adults on companion robot design.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post
University of Houston report on ELARA's community research

paragraphs.text: Chorong Park shared a behind-the-scenes account of an interview with KHOU 11 reporter Amanda Henderson on September 3, 2026. The photographs show filming and community activities at the Mamie George Community Center.

The update places older adults' perspectives at the center of ELARA's work. Park described listening to what people find welcoming, useful, confusing, or intrusive when they encounter companion robots.

A University of Houston report by Kelly Schafler offers additional context: older adults and students have contributed feedback on existing robots and used creative activities to explore ideas for future designs. The work supports development, rather than establishing that a new robot has already been completed or clinically validated.

Park emphasized an aim of supporting choice, independence, and connection without replacing human relationships. She thanked community participants, students, and collaborators for helping shape the research.
At the time of her post, broadcast coverage was expected near the end of September. This article records the interview and preparation; it does not imply that the segment has already aired.
